new_entities.name: Long-term methylphenidate in children
aliases: long-term stimulant methylphenidate use in children
new_entities.description: Chronic methylphenidate treatment in children with ADHD over months to years.

new_entities.name: Growth velocity
new_entities.description: Rate of height or weight gain over time during childhood treatment.

edges.effect_quant: A 2011 review summarized randomized and systematic-review evidence suggesting methylphenidate slows growth by about 1 to 1.5 cm per year during treatment, and long-term observational data have repeatedly found reduced weight and height trajectories during chronic stimulant exposure, although some catch-up growth may occur after discontinuation.
edges.population: children and adolescents receiving long-term methylphenidate treatment for ADHD
edges.mechanism: Chronic stimulant therapy can reduce appetite, alter energy balance, and suppress expected height and weight gain during active treatment periods.
edges.summary: Long-term methylphenidate has a real growth tradeoff signal in children. The average effect is usually modest rather than catastrophic, but slower height and weight gain during treatment is a consistent enough finding to treat as a meaningful harm signal that warrants monitoring.
edges.caveats: This does not mean every treated child will have clinically important growth suppression, and some children show later catch-up. The clearest message is to monitor growth rather than to deny treatment benefit.

evidence.citation: Findling RL et al 2007 J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry
evidence.notes: Long-term effects of methylphenidate transdermal delivery system treatment of ADHD on growth.

evidence.citation: Vater CH et al 2023 J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol
evidence.notes: Growth Trajectories in Stimulant Treated Children and Adolescents: A Qualitative Review of the Literature from Comprehensive Datasets and Registries.
